title_en: Shanghai Minhang District People's Procuratorate v. Bian Fei — illegal business operations case
ruling_gist_en: When determining illegal business operations, the people's court shall base its decision on administrative laws and regulations. With respect to internal documents of administrative organs, the court must comprehensively review whether they comply with relevant provisions of administrative laws and regulations, and shall not solely rely on such documents to find that the actor's conduct constitutes a crime.

full_text_en:
Shanghai Minhang District People's Procuratorate v. Bian Fei — illegal business operations

Ruling Summary

When a people's court determines whether an act constitutes illegal business operations, it shall base its decision on the provisions of administrative laws and regulations. Internal documents of administrative agencies shall be comprehensively reviewed to determine whether they comply with the relevant provisions of administrative laws and regulations, and shall not be used alone as the basis for finding that the actor's conduct constitutes a crime.

Procuratorial Authority: Shanghai Minhang District People's Procuratorate

Defendant: Bian Fei, male, Han ethnicity, born in October 1958, legal representative of Shanghai Huihai Electronic Equipment Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Pearl Medical Technology Development Co., Ltd., residing in Guangling District, Yangzhou City, Jiangsu Province. He was criminally detained on April 26, 2017, on suspicion of illegal business operations, released on bail pending further investigation on June 1, 2017, arrested on December 8, 2017, and released on bail pending further investigation on December 9, 2017.

The Shanghai Minhang District People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution against the defendant Bian Fei for the crime of illegal business operations before the Shanghai Minhang District People's Court.

The indictment alleged: From July 2015, the defendant Bian Fei, in the course of operating Shanghai Huihai Electronic Equipment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Huihai Company"), produced bio-energy instruments of models SE-F1, SE-F2, and SE-F3 series, which were sold by Shanghai Pearl Medical Technology Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Pearl Company"). A total of 182 SE-series bio-energy instruments were produced and sold, with a total amount of RMB 924,270. Upon a reply letter from the National Medical Products Administration (hereinafter "NMPA"), it was determined that the SE-series bio-energy instruments fall under Class II medical devices. The "Inspection Report" issued by the National Infrared and Industrial Electric Heating Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Center (Wuhan Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Institute) tested the relative radiation energy spectrum (infrared radiation wavelength range) of the SE bio-energy instruments and the Harbin Quanke therapeutic instrument. In December 2016, administrative law enforcement authorities seized 127 involved SE-series bio-energy instruments, valued at RMB 581,740. Bian Fei, in violation of state regulations, operated without a license to deal in goods subject to restricted sale under laws and administrative regulations, disrupting market order, and the circumstances were serious. His conduct constituted the crime of illegal business operations. The procuratorate requested the court to convict Bian Fei in accordance with Article 225(1), Article 231, Article 30, and Article 31 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

The defendant Bian Fei argued: The products involved in the case were qualified household appliances, not medical devices, and his business operations were lawful and did not constitute the crime of illegal business operations.

The defense counsel submitted the following opinions: The Administrative Ruling of Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court [(2017) Jing Xing Chu No. 502] held that the reply letter was essentially an exchange of views between the defendant and the Shanghai Municipal Drug Administration (hereinafter "Shanghai Drug Administration") on the specific application of the law and did not establish new rights or obligations, and it had no legally binding effect on the Minhang Market Regulatory Bureau's determination of the plaintiff's conduct in producing SE bio-energy instruments. The reply letter was not a legal basis for deeming the involved SE bio-energy instruments as Class II medical devices. Huihai Company only sold the products involved through ordinary household appliance channels, did not enter any medical institutions, and did not engage in any medical device advertising. Medical devices are items that can be operated after review and are not state-monopolized or restricted-sale items requiring special state licensing. It was clearly inappropriate to apply the crime of illegal business operations, and the defendant Bian Fei should be acquitted.

The Shanghai Minhang District People's Court found the following facts at first instance:

The defendant Bian Fei was the legal representative of Huihai Company and Pearl Company. Huihai Company's business scope included the sale of electronic equipment and electronic products, and the assembly and sale of electronic health instruments (excluding medical devices). Pearl Company's business scope included medical devices, healthcare, and biological products. Starting from July 2015, Huihai Company began producing bio-energy instruments of models SE-F1, SE-F2, and SE-F3 series, which were sold by Pearl Company. In March 2016, the Shanghai Minhang District Market Regulatory Bureau (hereinafter "Minhang Market Regulatory Bureau") submitted a request to the Shanghai Drug Administration regarding whether the product should be managed as a medical device, and if so, under which class of medical device it should be registered, and whether the product had obtained a medical device product registration certificate. The request included the packaging and product photos of the SE bio-energy instrument, the instruction manual, and the original certificate of conformity. The Shanghai Drug Administration then sought guidance from the NMPA on whether the product should be managed as a Class II medical device. The NMPA replied that the intended purpose of the product met the requirements of Article 76 of the Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Medical Devices (State Council Order No. 650) and, in accordance with the Medical Device Classification Rules (CFDA Order No. 15), it should be managed as a Class II medical device.

In December 2016, the Minhang Market Regulatory Bureau, during on-site law enforcement, seized a total of 127 SE-series bio-energy instruments from Huihai Company's warehouse at No. 6, Lane 28, Chunzhong Road, Minhang District, and from Pearl Company's relevant sales points, with a total value of RMB 581,740.

According to an appraisal by Shanghai Hugang Jinmao Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd., as of the time of the incident, Huihai Company and Pearl Company had produced and sold a total of 182 SE-series bio-energy instruments, with a total amount of RMB 924,270.

The Shanghai Minhang District People's Court held at first instance:

Under the Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Medical Devices, the state implements classified management of medical devices according to risk levels. Class I low-risk medical devices are subject to record-filing management, while Class II medium-risk medical devices and Class III high-risk medical devices are subject to product registration management, meaning that the production and sale of Class II and Class III medical devices require administrative licensing. The prosecutorial authority in this case argued that the SE bio-energy instrument is a Class II medical device and requires a medical device product registration certificate for production and operation. In contrast, the defendant Bian Fei argued that the SE bio-energy instrument is a qualified household appliance and does not require administrative licensing for production and sale. The court, upon trial, found that the prosecutorial authority's charge that Bian Fei committed the crime of illegal business operations under Article 225(1) of the Criminal Law could not be established. The reasons are as follows:

1. Insufficient evidence to establish the nature of the involved device

The crime of illegal business operations is an administrative crime. When hearing a case, the judicial authority must first determine whether the actor's conduct has violated administrative laws and regulations. According to the administrative law principles of "what is not prohibited by law is permitted" and "what is not specified by law is not punishable," an actor's conduct that is not explicitly prohibited or identified as illegal by law or regulation is not an illegal act.

The involved SE bio-energy instrument is a new type of product not included in the medical device catalog. The administrative authority's determination of its nature must comply with basic principles.

First, administrative licensing must comply with the basic requirement of the principle of administrative openness. Information such as the items, basis, conditions, quantity, procedures, time limits for administrative licensing, as well as the complete list of materials required from applicants and model texts of application forms, must be disclosed to ensure the public's right to know. According to the Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Medical Devices, the drug regulatory authority under the State Council is responsible for formulating the classification rules and classification catalog for medical devices, which must be published to the public. However, according to the medical device classification catalog published by the NMPA at the time of the incident, as well as the revised medical device classification catalog published by the NMPA on December 31, 2017, and effective January 1, 2018, the involved SE bio-energy instrument was not included as a medical device at the time of the incident or during the trial. The reply stating "should be managed as a Class II medical device" is different from the concept of "has been included." The court held that only after the involved item is included in the medical device catalog, its definition is clarified by the NMPA, and the corresponding normative documents are made public, can legal liability be imposed on actors who produce or operate "without a license." The reply letter is an exchange of views between the NMPA and the Shanghai Drug Administration on related issues, and it is an internal document of an administrative agency without external effect; it cannot serve as the basis for administrative penalties.

Second, determining the nature of a device must follow scientific and professional technical specifications and strictly adhere to existing regulations. According to the provisions of the Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Medical Devices regarding applications for registration of Class II and Class III medical devices, such medical devices require product inspection reports issued by medical device testing institutions and clinical trials conducted at qualified clinical trial institutions. Only testing institutions accredited by the certification and accreditation authority under the State Council, jointly with the drug regulatory authority under the State Council, may test medical devices. According to the NMPA's "Notice on Regulating the Classification of Medical Device Products," for classification confirmation of medical devices not yet listed in the "Classification Catalog" or other notification documents encountered in daily supervision or complaint reporting, provincial drug regulatory departments shall submit a request to the NMPA, together with relevant detailed information supporting classification and a pre-classification opinion. The NMPA shall then organize the Medical Device Standardization Management Center to study and determine the classification. In this case, the reply letter issued by the NMPA based on materials such as product packaging, photos, instruction manuals, and certificates of conformity submitted by the Shanghai Drug Administration, as well as the "Inspection Report" issued by the National Infrared and Industrial Electric Heating Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Center (Wuhan Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Institute), cannot substitute for an inspection report from a qualified medical device testing institution. The prosecutorial authority also failed to provide evidence that the testing unit had the qualification for medical device testing, nor did the NMPA provide other materials such as technical testing of the physical object, expert review, or assessment conclusions. Therefore, the evidence on record is insufficient to prove that the SE bio-energy instrument is a Class II medical device.

2. Insufficient evidence to establish the defendant Bian Fei's criminal intent

The whistleblower, Harbin Quanke Medical Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Quanke Company"), claimed in its report that the SE bio-energy instrument and Quanke Company's product were highly similar in appearance and had consistent promotional product functions. It argued that the defendant Bian Fei knew that Quanke Company's product was a Class II medical device, so he should have known that the SE bio-energy instrument was also a medical device. Quanke Company's statement is a subjective opinion and judgment. In the absence of other objective evidence to corroborate it, the self-provided comparison explanation cannot serve as proof. Therefore, the evidence on record is insufficient to prove that Bian Fei had the subjective intent to illegally operate Class II medical devices.

In summary, the existing evidence cannot prove that the defendant Bian Fei had the subjective intent to illegally operate Class II medical devices and objectively carried out the above conduct. The prosecutorial authority's charge that Bian Fei committed the crime of illegal business operations lacks sufficient evidence, and the charge cannot be established. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, the Shanghai Minhang District People's Court rendered the following judgment on November 13, 2019:

The defendant Bian Fei is acquitted.

After the first-instance judgment, the defendant Bian Fei did not appeal, but the prosecutorial authority, the Shanghai Minhang District People's Procuratorate, filed a protest.

The Shanghai Minhang District People's Procuratorate in its protest argued that the first-instance defendant Bian Fei's conduct constituted the crime of illegal business operations and that the first-instance judgment finding Bian Fei not guilty was erroneous. The main reasons were as follows: 1. The reply letter "On the Classification of SE Bio-Energy Instrument Products" issued by the General Office of the NMPA was legally obtained and objective in content, confirming that the SE bio-energy instrument is a Class II medical device, and the evidence on record corroborates the NMPA's classification basis. 2. Bian Fei has a medical background and is familiar with relevant industry laws and regulations. He should have known that the SE bio-energy instrument he produced and operated required relevant access procedures for Class II medical devices, which he failed to obtain, indicating subjective intent for illegal business operations. 3. Bian Fei violated state regulations by producing and selling Class II medical devices, which should have been under regulatory oversight, in the guise of ordinary household appliances, evading administrative authorities' review, evaluation, and subsequent supervision of the safety of the involved products, seriously infringing on the rights of other legitimate products and disrupting the market order for medical devices, thereby having significant social harm and constituting the crime of illegal business operations.

The First Branch of the Shanghai People's Procuratorate expressed the opinion at the second instance that the first-instance judgment's findings of fact and application of law regarding the first-instance defendant Bian Fei's illegal business operations were erroneous, leading to an improper acquittal. It considered the Minhang District Procuratorate's protest opinion correct and recommended that the second-instance court adopt it and render a judgment in accordance with the law. During the second instance, the procuratorial authority also provided and presented a reply letter obtained during the second instance, titled "Reply on the Entrusted Determination of SE Bio-Energy Instrument Series Products," issued by the Shanghai Drug Administration (hereinafter "Shanghai Drug Administration") to the Minhang District People's Procuratorate, to prove that Bian Fei's conduct constituted the crime of illegal business operations.

The first-instance defendant Bian Fei did not file an appeal but stated in court that his conduct did not constitute a crime.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, upon trial at second instance, confirmed the facts found at first instance. The evidence materials provided by the procuratorial authority at the second-instance trial were also subject to cross-examination in court.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

Regarding whether the first-instance defendant Bian Fei's conduct constituted the crime of illegal business operations. Upon investigation, Article 7(2) of the "Measures for the Connection between Administrative Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice in Food and Drug Matters" jointly issued by the NMPA, the Ministry of Public Security, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Food Safety Office of the State Council on December 22, 2015, stipulates that when a food and drug regulatory authority transfers a suspected criminal case to a public security authority, it shall attach the following materials: ... (4) relevant inspection reports or expert opinions. Meanwhile, Article 2 of the same Measures provides that these Measures apply to cases involving suspected violations or crimes in the fields of food (including food additives), drugs, medical devices, and cosmetics handled by food and drug regulatory authorities, public security authorities, people's procuratorates, and people's courts at all levels. In this case, the reply letter "On the Classification of SE Bio-Energy Instrument Products" issued by the General Office of the NMPA and the reply letter "On the Entrusted Determination of SE Bio-Energy Instrument Series Products" issued by the Shanghai Drug Administration only determined that the product should be managed as a Class II medical device based on the intended purpose stated in the instruction manual and other materials of the involved SE bio-energy instruments. However, they did not conduct physical inspection or expert evaluation of the seized products, nor did they clearly identify the specific type of Class II medical device to which the involved products belonged. Taking all evidence materials together, while it is sufficient to prove that Bian Fei, as a professional in the medical-related industry, had the subjective intention to circumvent legal oversight, it is still insufficient to prove that the involved SE bio-energy instrument is a Class II medical device. Therefore, the evidence to find Bian Fei's conduct constitutes the crime of illegal business operations is insufficient.

In conclusion, the first-instance court's finding that the first-instance defendant Bian Fei was not guilty was accurate in nature, correct in the application of law, and the trial procedure was lawful. The protest opinion of the protesting authority and the second-instance procuratorial authority's opinion supporting the protest are not adopted. Accordingly, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 236(1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following ruling on November 25, 2020:

The protest is dismissed and the original judgment is sustained.

This ruling is final.
